facts_of_case: Petitioner filed a petition under Section 125 Cr.P.C. and an FIR under various sections against the respondent due to matrimonial discord.

legal_principles.principle: While deciding the transfer application, courts should give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of female litigants.
legal_principles.held: The Courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of the female litigants and transfer of legal proceedings from one Court to another should ordinarily be allowed, taking into consideration their convenience and the Courts should desist from putting female litigants under undue hardships.
cited_cases: Sumita Singh Vs. Kumar Sanjay, (2002) SC 396
Rajani Kishor Pardeshi Vs. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) (12) SCC 237

legal_principles.principle: In matrimonial matters, courts should consider the economic soundness of both parties, their social strata, behavioural pattern, standard of life prior to and subsequent to marriage, and circumstances of both parties in eking out their livelihood.
legal_principles.held: The Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya Vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

outcome.final_order: The trial court was directed to transfer the petition filed by the respondent-husband from Faridabad to Palwal.

keywords: Latin Maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
